title: Price your packages, pitch well and agree in writing
course_title: Freelancing Fundamentals: Package, Price and Deliver Paid Work

say: Price your packages, pitch well, and agree every job in writing.
This is the video for module two of Freelancing Fundamentals.
Clients rarely want to buy hours. They want a finished result. But behind every price you need one number only you see: your minimum hourly rate.

panel.heading: From a skill to a paid job

say: You will turn your service into packages the client can choose from.

panel.heading: From a skill to a paid job

say: You will learn a short pitch that gets replies.

panel.heading: From a skill to a paid job

say: And you will agree every job in writing before you start.

panel.heading: From a skill to a paid job

say: Your minimum rate is the lowest amount per working hour that keeps your business alive. Here is how Amaka works it out.
First, her income target. She wants to take home about 250,000 naira a month.
Second, she adds business costs: data, power and fuel, and saving for a laptop. That is 40,000.
Together that is 290,000 naira.
Third, she divides by her 72 billable hours. That is about 4,028 naira, which she rounds up to 4,100 an hour.
Twenty descriptions take her about 8 hours with checks and a revision. 8 times 4,100 is 32,800, so she prices the package at 35,000 naira.
Three sizes help the client choose how much to buy, instead of whether to buy at all. Basic is 10 descriptions for about 18,000 naira.
Standard is 20 descriptions for about 35,000. Many clients pick the middle package, so make it the one you most want to sell.
Premium adds more work and a second revision round, for about 55,000. Check every price against your minimum rate.
Each package should also say what is outside it, for example product photography not included. This protects you when a small extra is really a new job.
The goal of one message is not to close a sale. It is to get a reply.
For example, Ifeoma in Enugu wrote to a home bakery. She noticed their cake posts had no prices or ordering steps.

panel.heading: The four-part pitch
items: Ask for a small next step

say: She offered one service: short Instagram captions that include the price, size and a simple order step.

panel.heading: The four-part pitch
items: Ask for a small next step

say: She showed proof with one sample link, not her whole life story.

panel.heading: The four-part pitch
items: Ask for a small next step

say: And she asked for a tiny yes: may I rewrite three of your captions, at no cost? Keep free samples small, about 30 to 45 minutes at most.

panel.heading: The four-part pitch
items: Ask for a small next step

say: Busy people miss messages. Follow up once after 3 or 4 days, send a final note about a week later, then move on. Respect any no immediately.

panel.heading: The four-part pitch
items: Ask for a small next step
panel.rule: Follow up after 3 or 4 days, once more, then stop

say: After a short discovery call, where you ask more and talk less, send a written scope the same day. Scope means exactly what work is included.
List the deliverables, what the client provides, the deadline and revisions, what is not included, the price and payment terms, and who owns the final work.
End with: if this is correct, please reply Agreed and send the deposit, and I will start.
A clear Agreed in writing is your record of the deal.

panel.heading: No deposit, no start
items: Deposit confirmed in your own app

say: A deposit is part payment before you start. Many freelancers ask new clients for 50 percent up front, and the balance before final files.

panel.heading: No deposit, no start
items: Deposit confirmed in your own app

say: Only then does paid work begin.

panel.heading: No deposit, no start
items: Deposit confirmed in your own app

say: Watch for scope creep, when a job slowly grows through small extra requests. Zainab in Abuja agreed 12 posts for 60,000 naira. When the client asked for a flyer and 3 more posts, she sent a change request for 27,000 naira, and the client agreed.

panel.heading: No deposit, no start
items: Deposit confirmed in your own app
panel.rule: Answer every extra request kindly, then price it

say: To remember. Your rate is your target plus costs, divided by billable hours. Price packages from your hours, rounded up.
Pitch in four short parts. Get a written scope and a deposit before work. And price every extra request.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Package price = hours x rate, rounded up
Pitch: notice, offer, proof, small step
Written scope and deposit before work

say: Now build your price sheet with three packages, send your first ten pitches, and create your scope template.
